address: 196-35 Peck Avenue
description_html:
DSNY holds pop-up e-waste and textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City.

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics.

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

Learn more about this event.

Experience the Sun like never before with local astronomer Novaughn Miller during this fascinating afternoon of safe solar observation. Using specially filtered telescopes, participants will get an up-close view of the Sun's surface while learning about sunspots, solar activity, and the science behind our closest star. This family-friendly program is a unique opportunity to explore astronomy in the heart of Fort Tryon Park.
All viewing equipment is equipped with certified solar filters, making the experience completely safe for your eyes. As the program takes place outdoors during the warmest part of the day, attendees are encouraged to dress for the weather, wear sunscreen, bring water, and consider a hat for sun protection.
Sunday, August 23
4:00 p.m.
Cloisters Lawn

description_html:
Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.

For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. address: Reading Room in Bryant Park
description_html: Join us at Reel Talks for a conversation on Eyes Wide Shut with author Megan Abbott and host Scott Adlerberg.<br \/>Megan Abbott is the award-winning author of twelve crime novels, including You Will Know Me, Beware the Woman, and the New York Times bestseller The Turnout, winner of the Los Angeles Times Book Prize. She is also a screenwriter and the co-creator of Dare Me, the series she adapted from her own novel, now streaming on Netflix. She is currently adapting her latest novel, the national bestseller El Dorado Drive, for television for A24.<br \/>Scott Adlerberg is the author of five novels, including Graveyard Love, Jack Waters, and The Screaming Child.  He has written many short stories and contributes pieces regularly to sites such as CrimeReads and Mystery Tribune.  He was born in New York City and lives in Brooklyn.<br \/>
short_description: Talks on movies, the culture of cinema, and filmmaking.

description_html: Join Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland and floodplain restoration. Dates include Wednesdays weekly from August 5th - August 26th. Dates are 8\/5, 8\/12, 8\/19, and 8\/26. All sessions run 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM.<br \/>August 5 and August 12: hand removal of invasive water chestnut on Van Cortlandt Lake, from shore and from boats. August 19 and August 26: cutting invasive common reed (Phragmites) and clearing the floodplain edge. Wear clothes that can get wet and muddy; long sleeves and boots recommended for the August 19 and 26 sessions.<br \/>Meet outside the VCPA offices at the Van Cortlandt Golf House, next to the bathrooms. Tools, gloves and training provided. No experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Registration required. Groups of 6 or more, please email <a href=\"mailto:noel@vancortlandt.org\">noel@vancortlandt.org<\/a> in advance.<br \/>

address: Randall's Island Park
description_html: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall's Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall's Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.<br \/>Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.<br \/>Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. address: VCPA Learning Garden in Van Cortlandt Park
description_html:
Be a part of the community effort to maintain the trails in Van Cortlandt Park. Whether you're an experienced trailblazer or new to trail maintenance, your help will make a significant impact!
Meeting Details:
Location: VCPA Learning Garden - 6000 Mosholu Ave, Bronx, NY 10471. Across from the Riverdale Stables.
Time: 9 am sharp; work begins at 9:15 am.
Upcoming Activities Include:
Clearing debris and overgrowth
Ensuring trail safety and accessibility
Desire line closures
What to Bring:
Comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing
Closed-toed shoes
Water and a snack
Why Join Us?
Contribute to the vitality and safety of the trails you love! Engage with fellow community members, learn about trail maintenance, and enjoy the satisfaction of hands-on work in the great outdoors.
Necessary tools and gloves will be provided!
Want to bring a group? This event is limited to small groups of 5 or less. If you would like to bring more 6 or more ...

description_html:
DSNY holds pop-up e-waste and textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City.

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics. 

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

Learn more about this event.

address: Ferry Point Parking Lot- Off of Hutchinson River Parkway in Ferry Point Park
description_html: Volunteer with NYC Parks for Trees Count 2025! At each event you will receive a tote bag with all the materials needed to count trees. Next, we'll provide a 30-minute training session that includes the basics of tree identification and how to measure and assess each tree. Using our Tree Census app, you’ll split up into different zones within the park to start counting trees! After completing your first training event, you are welcome to continue counting trees on your own in smaller parks across the city. Registration is required. Registration begins on August 15.<\/p>

description_html: The Only Plane in the Sky reconstructs the harrowing events of 9\/11 minute-by-minute through the voices of those who lived it-passengers, air traffic controllers, first responders, military leaders, and government officials-creating an immersive oral history of a single shattering day. These first-hand accounts paint the picture of a country realizing it was under attack, and the title reflects the haunting moment when all civilian aircraft were grounded, leaving Air Force One as the only plane left in the sky. Just nine days before the 25th anniversary of the attacks, Graff revisits that harrowing morning, honoring its dark legacy while exploring how those hours permanently reshaped our national identity, America's innocence, and generations to come.<br \/>Garrett M. Graff is a bestselling journalist and Pulitzer Prize finalist historian who has covered politics, technology, and national security for two decades.
